title: Idempotency & Concurrency Control in Distributed Workers with Go & Redis
summary: Reliable message processing with Distributed Locks, Dedup Keys, and graceful failure handling without goroutine leaks.
author: Tan Huynh Nhat

sections.problem-statement: In distributed worker architectures, messaging systems (RabbitMQ, Kafka) operate on At-Least-Once delivery semantics. During transient network hiccups or consumer pod restarts, payment and order update messages can be delivered multiple times, risking race conditions and duplicate financial deductions.
sections.initial-approach: A simple "Check-then-Act" pattern checks database state prior to execution. In multi-worker environments, however, concurrent goroutines frequently read the "PENDING" status simultaneously, both proceeding to process the duplicate event and corrupting state.
sections.optimization-thinking:
We engineered a resilient, two-tiered idempotency model:

  • Distributed Locks via Redis: Atomic SET lock_key worker_id NX PX 5000 operations ensure only a single worker executes the transaction block for a specific deduplication key.
  • Atomic State Transitions: Database updates enforce conditional state guards: UPDATE orders SET status = 'PAID' WHERE id = ? AND status = 'PENDING'.
  • Graceful Shutdown: Goroutine lifecycles are bound to sync.WaitGroup and cancelable contexts, preventing abrupt termination of in-flight business transactions.
sections.code-implementation:
Go implementation of the idempotent distributed worker:

func (w *PaymentWorker) Process(ctx context.Context, msg Message) error {
    lockKey := fmt.Sprintf("lock:payment:%s", msg.PaymentID)
    acquired, err := w.redis.SetNX(ctx, lockKey, w.workerID, 10*time.Second).Result()
    if err != nil || !acquired {
        return nil // Skip processing if another worker holds the lock
    }
    defer w.redis.Del(ctx, lockKey)

    return w.db.Transaction(func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
        res, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, "UPDATE payments SET status = 'COMPLETED' WHERE id = ? AND status = 'PENDING'", msg.PaymentID)
        if err != nil { return err }
        rows, _ := res.RowsAffected()
        if rows == 0 { return nil } // Already processed idempotently
        return w.dispatchReceipt(ctx, msg)
    })
}
sections.complexity-applications: Time Complexity: O(1) Redis lock acquisition and O(1) indexed SQL execution. Widely applicable to e-commerce payment gateways, financial ledger syncs, ticketing platforms, and mission-critical event-driven architectures.
